title: 2 Samuel Chapter 24 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on 2 Samuel chapter 24 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: 2 Samuel Chapter 24 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of 2 Samuel Chapter 24.

questions.question: Who was moved by the LORD to number Israel and Judah?
questions.correctAnswer: David
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 24:1 states that the LORD moved David against Israel to say, 'Go, number Israel and Judah.'

questions.question: To whom did King David give the command to number the tribes of Israel?
questions.correctAnswer: Joab
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 24:2 records that David said to Joab, the captain of the host, to number the people.

questions.question: From where to where was Joab instructed to number the people?
questions.correctAnswer: From Dan to Beersheba
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 24:2 specifies the tribes to be numbered were from Dan even to Beersheba.

questions.question: What was Joab's initial reaction to the king's command to number the people?
options: He encouraged the king and obeyed immediately
He questioned why the king delighted in this thing
He refused to obey the king's command
He suggested a different plan for numbering
questions.correctAnswer: He questioned why the king delighted in this thing
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 24:3 shows Joab questioning the king, asking why he delighted in numbering the people.

questions.question: True or False: Joab and the captains obeyed the king's word and went out to number the people of Israel.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 24:4 states that the king's word prevailed and Joab and the captains went out to number the people.

questions.question: Where did Joab and his men pitch their camp after passing over the Jordan River?
questions.correctAnswer: Aroer
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 24:5 mentions they pitched in Aroer on the right side of the city in the midst of the river of Gad.

questions.question: Which location is NOT mentioned as part of the area Joab and his men traveled through during the census?
questions.correctAnswer: Jericho
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 24:6-7 lists Danjaan, Zidon, and Tyre but does not mention Jericho.

questions.question: True or False: Joab and his men traveled through all cities of the Hivites and Canaanites during the census.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 24:7 says they came to the stronghold of Tyre and all the cities of the Hivites and Canaanites.

questions.question: How long did it take Joab and his men to complete the census and return to Jerusalem?
questions.correctAnswer: Nine months and twenty days
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 24:8 states that they came to Jerusalem at the end of nine months and twenty days.

questions.question: According to the census, how many valiant men that drew the sword were there in Israel?
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 24:9 reports that there were 800,000 valiant men in Israel who drew the sword.

questions.question: True or False: The number of men in Judah according to the census was 500,000.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 24:9 states that the men of Judah were 500,000.

questions.question: What was Joab's title as mentioned in the chapter?
questions.correctAnswer: Captain of the host
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 24:2 identifies Joab as the captain of the host with the king.

questions.question: Which river did Joab and his men cross to begin the census journey?
questions.correctAnswer: Jordan
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 24:5 says they passed over Jordan and pitched in Aroer.

questions.question: True or False: The king's command to number the people prevailed over Joab's objections.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 24:4 confirms that although Joab objected, the king's word prevailed and the census was conducted.

questions.question: In 2 Samuel 24, which instruction comes first?
options: Joab is told to number the people
David prays to the LORD for forgiveness
Gad offers David three choices of punishment
David buys the threshingfloor of Araunah
questions.correctAnswer: Joab is told to number the people
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 24:2 shows that the first instruction is David commanding Joab to number the people; the other events occur later.

medium.title: 2 Samuel Chapter 24 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from 2 Samuel Chapter 24 to real-life situations.

questions.question: Why did David feel remorse after numbering the people of Israel and Judah?
options: Because he realized he had sinned greatly in doing it
Because the people were angry with him
Because the number was smaller than expected
questions.correctAnswer: Because he realized he had sinned greatly in doing it
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 24:10 states that David's heart smote him after numbering the people, and he confessed to the LORD that he had sinned greatly and done foolishly.

questions.question: Who delivered God's message to David offering him three punishments to choose from?
questions.correctAnswer: Gad the prophet
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 24:11-12 explains that the word of the LORD came to Gad, David's seer, who was sent to deliver God's offer of three punishments to David.

questions.question: Which of the following options was NOT one of the three punishments Gad presented to David?
options: Three months of fleeing from enemies
questions.correctAnswer: Seven days of drought
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 24:13 lists the three punishments as seven years of famine, three months fleeing enemies, and three days of pestilence; drought is not mentioned.

questions.question: How does David’s response to Gad’s message demonstrate a biblical virtue?
options: He shows trust in God's mercy by choosing to fall into His hand rather than man's
He blames his soldiers for the sin
He tries to negotiate for less punishment
questions.correctAnswer: He shows trust in God's mercy by choosing to fall into His hand rather than man's
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 24:14 shows David expressing great faith and trust in God's mercy over human hands, emphasizing reliance on God's compassion.

questions.question: What was the outcome of God sending the pestilence on Israel?
options: Seventy thousand men died from Dan to Beersheba
questions.correctAnswer: Seventy thousand men died from Dan to Beersheba
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 24:15 records that the pestilence caused the death of seventy thousand men throughout Israel, from Dan to Beersheba.

questions.question: True or False: The angel of the LORD completed the destruction of Jerusalem before the LORD stopped him.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 24:16 explains that the LORD repented of the evil and told the angel to stay his hand before Jerusalem was destroyed.

questions.question: What does David’s plea in 2 Samuel 24:17 teach us about humility and intercession?
options: David accepts personal guilt and asks for punishment on himself instead of the people
David blames the people for the punishment
David ignores the plague and continues ruling
David prays for his enemies to be punished
questions.correctAnswer: David accepts personal guilt and asks for punishment on himself instead of the people
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 24:17 shows David confessing his sin and pleading for the LORD to let the punishment fall on him and his family rather than on the innocent people, demonstrating humility and intercession.

questions.question: According to 2 Samuel 24:18, what command did Gad give to David regarding the plague?
options: To build an altar to the LORD on the threshingfloor of Araunah
To gather the army for battle
To offer sacrifices in the temple
questions.correctAnswer: To build an altar to the LORD on the threshingfloor of Araunah
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 24:18 states that Gad instructed David to go up and rear an altar unto the LORD on the threshingfloor of Araunah the Jebusite.

questions.question: What does the timing of Gad’s command in verse 18 suggest about God’s plan to stop the plague?
options: The plague would cease when the altar was built and offerings made
The plague would continue regardless of the altar
The altar was only symbolic and had no effect
The plague would end after seven years
questions.correctAnswer: The plague would cease when the altar was built and offerings made
questions.explanation: Verses 18, 24-25 show that building the altar and offering sacrifices was the way God provided for the plague to be stopped, linking the command to the outcome.

questions.question: What attitude did David demonstrate by insisting on buying the threshingfloor and oxen from Araunah instead of accepting them for free?
options: Integrity and respect for the LORD’s offerings
questions.correctAnswer: Integrity and respect for the LORD’s offerings
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 24:24 shows David’s refusal to offer to God what cost him nothing, demonstrating integrity and reverence in worship by paying the full price.

questions.question: True or False: Araunah gave all the materials for the altar to David as a generous gift.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 24:22-23 records that Araunah offered oxen, threshing instruments, and wood freely to David, showing generosity.

questions.question: How does the narrative of 2 Samuel 24 teach about the importance of repentance and prayer in times of crisis?
options: David’s sincere confession and prayer lead to God’s mercy and the stopping of the plague
Prayer had no effect and God’s judgment continued
David ignored repentance and continued sinning
questions.correctAnswer: David’s sincere confession and prayer lead to God’s mercy and the stopping of the plague
questions.explanation: Verses 10, 17, and 25 show David’s repentance, prayer, and sacrifice resulting in God being intreated and the plague ceasing, highlighting the power of humility and supplication.

questions.question: What does 2 Samuel 24:16 reveal about God’s character in relation to judgment?
options: God is merciful and can relent from sending calamity
God is rigid and never changes His mind
God always destroys completely without mercy
God is indifferent to human suffering
questions.correctAnswer: God is merciful and can relent from sending calamity
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 24:16 shows that when the angel was about to destroy Jerusalem, the LORD repented and told the angel to stay his hand, demonstrating God’s mercy.

questions.question: True or False: David’s choice to trust God rather than man in verse 14 shows a biblical application of faith during hardship.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 24:14 records David’s expression of trust in God's mercy instead of human intervention, exemplifying faith in adversity.

questions.question: What lesson about godly leadership is illustrated by David’s actions in 2 Samuel 24:17?
options: Accepting responsibility and interceding for the people
questions.correctAnswer: Accepting responsibility and interceding for the people
questions.explanation: In verse 17, David acknowledges his sin and asks God to let the punishment fall on him and his family rather than the people, showing responsible and sacrificial leadership.

hard.title: 2 Samuel Chapter 24 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from 2 Samuel Chapter 24.

questions.question: What was David's response when he saw the angel striking down the people?
options: He asked God to strike him and his family instead
He fled from the city in fear
He prayed for the immediate end of the plague
He commanded Joab to stop the counting of the people
questions.correctAnswer: He asked God to strike him and his family instead
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 24:17 shows David saying, 'let thine hand, I pray thee, be against me, and against my father's house,' indicating his willingness to bear the punishment instead of the people.

questions.question: Who instructed David to build an altar on the threshing floor of Araunah the Jebusite?
questions.correctAnswer: Gad the prophet
questions.explanation: According to 2 Samuel 24:18, Gad came to David and instructed him to build an altar at Araunah's threshing floor.

questions.question: How did Araunah show respect when he saw David approaching with his servants?
options: He ran to meet David with oxen
He bowed himself on his face upon the ground
He sent a messenger to greet David
He prepared a feast for David
questions.correctAnswer: He bowed himself on his face upon the ground
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 24:20 states that Araunah went out and bowed himself before the king on his face upon the ground as a sign of respect.

questions.question: What reason did David give for buying the threshing floor from Araunah?
options: To build an altar and stop the plague
To use it for military training
To give it as a gift to the priests
questions.correctAnswer: To build an altar and stop the plague
questions.explanation: In 2 Samuel 24:21, David explained he came to buy the threshing floor to build an altar to the LORD so that the plague would be stayed from the people.

questions.question: What did Araunah offer David for the altar sacrifices?
options: Oxen for burnt offering and threshing instruments
questions.correctAnswer: Oxen for burnt offering and threshing instruments
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 24:22 records Araunah offering oxen for burnt sacrifice and the threshing instruments for wood to David.

questions.question: How did Araunah treat David's request to buy the threshing floor?
options: He gave it to David for free
He gave it as a gift but David insisted on paying
questions.correctAnswer: He gave it as a gift but David insisted on paying
questions.explanation: According to 2 Samuel 24:23-24, Araunah offered the things as a gift, but David refused to offer to God that which cost him nothing and bought them for fifty shekels of silver.

questions.question: What was the outcome after David built the altar and offered burnt offerings and peace offerings?
options: The plague continued for seven years
The LORD was intreated and the plague was stayed
David was punished for his actions
questions.correctAnswer: The LORD was intreated and the plague was stayed
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 24:25 says that after David built the altar and made offerings, the LORD was intreated for the land and the plague was stopped.

questions.question: What does the Hebrew term "threshingfloor" in this chapter symbolize in the context of David's repentance and God's mercy?
options: A place of judgment and purification
questions.correctAnswer: A place of judgment and purification
questions.explanation: The threshing floor, where separation of grain from chaff occurs, symbolizes judgment and purification. David's altar there represents seeking atonement, consistent with ancient Israelite symbolism (2 Samuel 24:18-25).

questions.question: Which other Old Testament passage recounts a similar story of a king's census leading to a plague and the building of an altar?
questions.correctAnswer: 1 Chronicles 21
questions.explanation: 1 Chronicles 21 parallels 2 Samuel 24 by recounting David's census, the resulting plague, and the altar built on Araunah's threshing floor.

questions.question: How does the theme of God's mercy in 2 Samuel 24:14 relate to the New Testament teaching in Romans 5:8?
options: Both emphasize God's mercy despite human sinfulness
Both focus on the importance of strict law-keeping
Both reject the idea of repentance
questions.correctAnswer: Both emphasize God's mercy despite human sinfulness
questions.explanation: David trusts God's mercy in 2 Samuel 24:14; similarly, Romans 5:8 shows God's love and mercy demonstrated while we were sinners, highlighting the continuity of divine compassion.

questions.question: What literary device is prominently displayed in the structure of 2 Samuel 24 regarding the census, plague, and altar?
questions.correctAnswer: Chiasm
questions.explanation: The chapter shows a chiasm: A (Census), B (Plague), A' (Altar/atonement), highlighting the theological progression and symmetry in the narrative (2 Samuel 24).

questions.question: True or False: David was content with Araunah giving the threshing floor and oxen as a gift and did not pay for them.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 24:24 shows David insisted on paying fifty shekels of silver, refusing to offer to God that which cost him nothing.

questions.question: True or False: The plague sent by the LORD killed seventy thousand men from Dan to Beersheba.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 24:15 states that seventy thousand men died from Dan to Beersheba due to the pestilence sent by the LORD.

questions.question: Which option best describes David's attitude when Gad offered him three punishments to choose from?
options: He chose to flee from his enemies
He preferred to fall into the LORD's hands because of His mercy
He asked for seven years of famine
He refused to choose any punishment
questions.correctAnswer: He preferred to fall into the LORD's hands because of His mercy
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 24:14 records David's choice to fall into the LORD's hands rather than men because God's mercies are great.

questions.question: What was Joab's initial reaction to David's command to number the people?
options: He questioned why the king delighted in doing this
He suggested a faster census method
questions.correctAnswer: He questioned why the king delighted in doing this
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 24:3 shows Joab asking why the king delighted in numbering the people, indicating his concern about the command.

theological.title: 2 Samuel Chapter 24 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from 2 Samuel Chapter 24 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What divine attribute is demonstrated when the LORD incited David to number Israel and Judah, as stated in 2 Samuel 24:1?
questions.correctAnswer: God’s holiness and justice
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 24:1 shows that the LORD's anger was kindled against Israel, prompting Him to move David to number the people. This reflects God's holiness and justice in responding to Israel's sin.

questions.question: What theological implication can be drawn from Joab's hesitation to carry out David's command to number Israel in 2 Samuel 24:3?
options: Joab understood God's blessing multiplies the people beyond mere numbers
Joab felt the census was a political act
questions.correctAnswer: Joab understood God's blessing multiplies the people beyond mere numbers
questions.explanation: In 2 Samuel 24:3, Joab says, 'Now the LORD thy God add unto the people, how many soever they be, an hundredfold,' showing his awareness that God's blessing is not limited to natural population but is supernaturally multiplied.

questions.question: How does the nine months and twenty days duration of the census journey (2 Samuel 24:8) emphasize the seriousness of David's sin?
options: It shows a prolonged act of disobedience and reliance on human strength
It indicates the census was well-planned
It demonstrates the joy of the people
questions.correctAnswer: It shows a prolonged act of disobedience and reliance on human strength
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 24:8 states the census took nine months and twenty days, indicating an extended period of focusing on numbers rather than trusting God, highlighting the seriousness of David's sin.

questions.question: What does the reported number of valiant men in Israel and Judah in 2 Samuel 24:9 teach about Israel's military strength and human confidence?
options: It reveals Israel's great military capacity which can lead to pride and misplaced confidence
It shows Israel was weak militarily
It indicates a small and humble nation
It reflects God's judgment on their numbers
questions.correctAnswer: It reveals Israel's great military capacity which can lead to pride and misplaced confidence
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 24:9 records 800,000 valiant men in Israel and 500,000 in Judah, highlighting the nation's significant military power that could foster pride and dependence on human might instead of God.

questions.question: What doctrine is illustrated by David’s confession of sin and plea for mercy in 2 Samuel 24:10?
options: The doctrine of repentance and divine mercy
The doctrine of justification by works
questions.correctAnswer: The doctrine of repentance and divine mercy
questions.explanation: David's confession in 2 Samuel 24:10, where he admits sin and asks the LORD to take away his iniquity, illustrates the doctrine of repentance and God’s merciful forgiveness.

questions.question: According to 2 Samuel 24:12-13, what theological principle is revealed through God offering David three punishments to choose from?
options: God’s justice balanced with mercy and human responsibility
questions.correctAnswer: God’s justice balanced with mercy and human responsibility
questions.explanation: In 2 Samuel 24:12-13, God presents David a choice among three punishments, displaying His justice but also mercy by allowing David to select, emphasizing human responsibility.

questions.question: What does David’s choice ‘to fall into the hand of the LORD’ in 2 Samuel 24:14 reveal about his understanding of God’s nature?
options: David trusts in God’s mercy rather than human wrath
David fears God more than man
questions.correctAnswer: David trusts in God’s mercy rather than human wrath
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 24:14 shows David choosing God’s judgment over man’s, affirming his trust in God’s mercy and compassion despite punishment.

questions.question: What attribute of God is shown in 2 Samuel 24:16 when the LORD commands the angel to stay his hand from destroying Jerusalem?
questions.correctAnswer: God’s mercy and sovereignty
questions.explanation: In 2 Samuel 24:16, God’s command to stop the angel reveals His sovereign control over judgment and His mercy in sparing Jerusalem from destruction.

questions.question: How does David’s intercession in 2 Samuel 24:17 demonstrate the biblical principle of substitutionary atonement?
options: David asks that punishment fall on him and his family instead of the people
questions.correctAnswer: David asks that punishment fall on him and his family instead of the people
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 24:17 shows David pleading that God’s hand be against him and his father’s house, typifying substitutionary atonement where one bears punishment for others.

questions.question: What theological significance does the location of the altar at the threshingfloor of Araunah in 2 Samuel 24:18-19 have in the redemptive narrative?
options: It foreshadows the future temple site and God’s provision for atonement
It marks a place of defeat
questions.correctAnswer: It foreshadows the future temple site and God’s provision for atonement
questions.explanation: The threshingfloor of Araunah in 2 Samuel 24:18-19 is significant as the site where David builds an altar, foreshadowing the temple’s location and God’s provision of atonement, linking to salvation history.

questions.question: What doctrinal truth about worship is revealed in David’s refusal to accept Araunah’s free gifts in 2 Samuel 24:24?
options: True worship requires costly sacrifice and genuine offering
Worship can be done with anything
questions.correctAnswer: True worship requires costly sacrifice and genuine offering
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 24:24 reveals David insisting on paying for the threshingfloor and oxen, teaching that genuine worship involves costly sacrifice and offering, not something received for free.

questions.question: How does 2 Samuel 24:25 demonstrate the efficacy of sacrifice in relation to God’s response to sin and judgment?
options: Sacrifices lead to the LORD being intreated and the plague being stayed
questions.correctAnswer: Sacrifices lead to the LORD being intreated and the plague being stayed
questions.explanation: In 2 Samuel 24:25, David’s offerings cause the LORD to be intreated, stopping the plague, showing that sacrificial acts can move God to mercy within the covenantal relationship.

questions.question: What combined teaching about divine judgment and human sinfulness is revealed by synthesizing 2 Samuel 24:1 and 2 Samuel 24:10?
options: God’s judgment is righteous, but repentance can restore favor
questions.correctAnswer: God’s judgment is righteous, but repentance can restore favor
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 24:1 shows God’s anger bringing judgment, while 2 Samuel 24:10 shows David’s repentance and plea for mercy, teaching that although God’s judgment is righteous, repentance restores His favor.

questions.question: What theological insight about God’s providence and human responsibility emerges from combining 2 Samuel 24:3 and 2 Samuel 24:14?
options: God multiplies His people graciously, but humans must trust Him rather than relying on their own plans
God limits the growth of His people
questions.correctAnswer: God multiplies His people graciously, but humans must trust Him rather than relying on their own plans
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 24:3 speaks of God adding to the people a hundredfold, and 2 Samuel 24:14 shows David choosing to fall into God’s hand, illustrating that God’s providence is gracious but demands human trust, not self-confidence.

questions.question: What does 2 Samuel 24:16-17 teach about God’s justice and mercy when the angel’s destruction is halted and David intercedes?
options: God’s justice can be mitigated by mercy through intercession
questions.correctAnswer: God’s justice can be mitigated by mercy through intercession
questions.explanation: Verses 16-17 show God halting the angel’s destruction and David interceding for the people, teaching that divine justice is balanced with mercy, which can be accessed through intercession.
